blockNote: Jeweler Gem: the Red Jewel collector NPC (Bank 08, 577187-577682). Placed with spawn parameter #01 in scenes $01 (South Cape), $32 (Freejia), $6B, $7B, $9B and $C3, one record each; every placement runs this same code.
=== SPAWN (code_08CEA3) ===

Event flag $E8 is the Solid Arm flag: sEA_solid_arm sets it, so after that optional fight Gem no longer appears (JewelerDie). The old header called it 'game complete'. Otherwise the spawn parameter in $0E picks an 8-frame animation group (all six records pass #01, which gives group 0): the animation index $28 is set to group x 8 + 2 (it is an animation index, not a sprite frame). $0E is then replaced by $3000, the OAM attribute word. Gem marks his tile solid, registers JewelerInteract as his chatPtr and idles on a bare RTL; the shared talk handler in global_ambient_dispatcher runs JewelerInteract when the player presses B facing him.
=== REWARD TIERS (JewelerInteract, JewelerCheck*) ===

JewelerInteract greets, prints the stored jewel count if it is non-zero and then walks the tiers in ascending order. A tier pays out when its 'given' flag is clear and jewelsCollected ($0AB0, a BCD value) has reached the threshold; each reward sets its flag and jumps to the next tier's check, so one talk can pay several tiers:
3 jewels (flag $E9): Herb, item #06. If GiveItem fails the inventory-full text is printed and the talk ends without setting the flag.
5 (flag $EA): playerDef + 1.
8 (flag $EB): playerMaxHp + 1 and hpToHeal = 1, so UpdateHUD adds one current HP and the new point is filled. It is not an HP-bar flash.
12 (flag $EC): playerStr + 1.
20 (flag $ED): $0B16 = 1, the Psycho Dash upgrade level (attack_ability_system reads it: damage 5 at level 0, 10 at level 1).
30 (flag $EE): $0B1C = 2, the Dark Friar upgrade level (damage 5 / 8 / 12; level 2 is the fully upgraded form).

50 (no flag): warp to scene $E9, the sE9_mansion_intro scene that leads to the optional Solid Arm fight. There is no 'given' flag, so every talk with 50 or more jewels warps again; the jewels are not consumed and the menu below is never reached.
The dialogue string for the 8-jewel tier says 'Your Life Power will be raised' and then 'Your Strength is raised by one'; the code raises max HP, so the second sentence is a text inconsistency.
=== MENU AND JEWEL COUNTING ===

After the cascade (and any payouts) Gem shows the three-option menu: Just wanted to see you / Give you Red Jewels / See your inventory. The DialogueOptions result table is indexed 0 = B cancel, 1..3 = the options in order, so cancel and option 1 share code_08CF59. 'Give you Red Jewels' (code_08CF5E) needs at least one item #01 in the inventory; JewelerCountJewels then counts the item #01 entries of the 16 inventory slots ($0AB4) with a BCD counter held in the absolute word $0000 (WRAM $7E:0000, scratch; not the actor's own DP $00), adds it to jewelsCollected in decimal mode, removes every jewel with RemoveItem in a loop and re-runs the tier check. 'See your inventory' prints the reward list and highlights (palette 4) each tier whose flag is set.
code_08D00D ('Well, see ya. Somewhere.') and its dialogue string have no reference anywhere: dead code.

blockNote: Reusable town door (Bank 00, 50675-50732). 16 placements in three scenes: $01 South Cape (5 doors), $32 Freejia (4) and $91 (7); fr32_guide spawns one more at runtime (SpawnAfterAbsFlags at TownDoorInit, X $0278, Y $0230). The old docs say '16 scenes'.

A door is drawn closed (frame #01 of spriteset_npc_props) and solid. When the player is next to it (BranchIfPlayerNear radius 1: both |dx| and |dy| within 16 px) and HOLDS UP (joypad $0800) for 8 consecutive frames, it plays SFX #0E on channel 2, clears its solid mark, switches to the open frame #00 and idles for the rest of the scene visit (nothing closes it again). The old header said 'A-button press'; the code tests the Up direction. Releasing Up or leaving the box restarts the count: the loop is re-entered through TownDoorProximityCheck and LoopStart reloads the counter.
A door that is already within radius 1 when it spawns skips the closed state: TownDoorInit branches straight to TownDoorOpenIdle, so it starts open (the player has just come out of the building).

Re-entry: after the first off-screen wait the entry pointer ($00) is the WaitWhileOffscreen op itself (it stores itself while the door is off-screen, which is the state at spawn because InitActorFromSceneData sets Flags10 bit $4000). Every later frame resumes there, passes straight through while on-screen and runs TownDoorProximityCheck. A door that is already on-screen at its first pass would instead be re-entered at AnimOnce and run the Init-time BranchIfPlayerNear to TownDoorOpenIdle first, which would open it without the Up hold; not verified at runtime (OQ-I043-1).

The solid mark: MarkSolidHere / ClearSolidHere OR and AND the high nibble of the collision cells under the actor's hitbox rectangle, not a single tile. The door itself is not a warp; the building entrance is a separate trigger.

partNotes.TownDoorInit: Door initialisation: closed frame #01, solid mark, start open if the player is already next to the door, then WaitWhileOffscreen (the loop head of later frames) and TownDoorProximityCheck.
partNotes.TownDoorProximityCheck: Per-frame test: player within 16 px on both axes -> TownDoorInteractLoop, otherwise end this pass (the entry pointer stays on WaitWhileOffscreen).
partNotes.TownDoorInteractLoop: Hold-Up loop: LoopStart sets a counter of 8, BranchIfPressed tests Up ($0800) every frame. Up not held: the count is lost (JumpNextFrame back to the proximity check, which re-enters here with a fresh counter). Up held for 8 consecutive frames: continue at TownDoorOpenAnim.
partNotes.TownDoorOpenAnim: LoopEnd (counts the held frame; after the 8th it falls through) and the door SFX #0E; falls into TownDoorOpenIdle where the frame actually changes.
partNotes.TownDoorOpenIdle: Open state: clear the solid mark, show the open frame #00 and idle on a bare RTL for the rest of the scene visit (nothing closes the door). Also the target when the player is already near at spawn.

blockNote: Grid-snap helper for COP SnapToGrid (#43) (Bank 0A, 697255-697341). It is not a function that is called: SnapToGrid saves the script's resume address in snapResumePtr ($7F1018) and the bank in $7F101A, then rewrites the COP return frame so that its RTI lands here, and ResumeAfterSnap (#4A) at the end restores them. SnapToGrid only redirects when ((X - 8) OR Y) AND $0F is non-zero; it first clears the movement override chain ($2C / $2E). The five script sites are av6D_steelbones (1), ec0C_ribber (1) and sg4D_cyber (3); the old header said it was 'called after spawning enemies'.

Targets: X = the nearest value that is 8 (mod 16), a tile centre (actor X is the centre, so the alignment test is (X - 8) AND $0F); Y = the nearest multiple of 16 (a tie at 8 rounds up). Both go to moveXAlt / moveYAlt and MoveToward (#FF, #01) glides there at 1 px per frame while keeping the current animation (#FF). #01 is a speed in px/frame, so the old 'max speed' wording was wrong and the glide is slow. When it ends the alignment is tested again and the targets are recomputed if the test fails (the actor was pushed or the glide was cut short).

The hit and dodge callbacks ($7F1000 / $7F1002) are cleared on entry so a hit or dodge cannot redirect the actor's entry pointer during the glide. Nothing in this routine restores them; the callers re-arm them later (ec0C_ribber and av6D_steelbones also write SetHitCallback #0000 around their snap).

697255.text: Clear the hit and dodge callbacks so no hit or dodge can redirect the actor's entry pointer during the glide

697266.text: Target X: nearest value that is 8 (mod 16), a tile centre; the alignment test uses (X - 8) AND $0F

697277.text: Upper half: floor16(v) + $18 = the next tile centre to the east

697286.text: Lower half: floor16(v) + $08 = this cell's tile centre

697297.text: Target Y: nearest multiple of 16 (the Y line); no centre offset on Y

697304.text: Upper half: floor16(Y) + $10 (a tie at 8 rounds up)

697320.text: Re-entry point = the MoveToward below (that COP yields every frame while it glides)

697322.text: Glide to (moveXAlt, moveYAlt): #FF = keep the current animation, speed 1 px per frame (not 'max speed')

697337.text: Not aligned (pushed, or the glide was cut short): recompute the targets

697339.text: Aligned: restore the script address and bank saved by SnapToGrid and continue the interrupted script
